_meta.title: LLM API pricing history 2024–2026
_meta.thesis: Across the major LLM API providers, prices dropped sharply in 2024–2025 and then stabilised. Here is the evidence — every confirmed event links to a dated Web Archive snapshot or public announcement. REVIEW: verify Wayback URLs and historical price figures before merge.
_meta.method: Curated from training data knowledge of public pricing announcements (2024-01 to 2026-06). Evidence URLs point to Wayback Machine captures where known. Some captures may need verification against live Wayback. Only CONFIRMED or widely-reported events are included; gaps and uncertainties are marked. Current (stable) prices sourced from llm/data/models.json (verified 2026-06-20).
_meta.note: REVIEW REQUIRED: Historical prices and Wayback URLs were generated from training data, not from live Wayback lookups. Owner should verify evidence URLs exist and historical price figures are correct before merge. Ceny = stop-and-confirm.

tools.name: OpenAI
tools.headline: Three major price generations in two years; costs down 90%+ vs GPT-4 launch

events.title: GPT-4 API launch — $30 / $60 per 1M tokens (8k context)
events.detail: GPT-4 launched with $0.03 per 1k input tokens ($30/1M) and $0.06 per 1k output tokens ($60/1M) for the 8k context window model. The 32k context variant was priced at $0.06 / $0.12 per 1k. These were the highest list prices OpenAI published for a text model at the time.

events.title: GPT-4 Turbo launch — input price cut 3x to $10/1M; GPT-3.5-Turbo cut ~10x
events.detail: GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview) launched at $0.01 / $0.03 per 1k tokens ($10 input / $30 output per 1M). The existing GPT-4 model kept its old price. GPT-3.5-Turbo was simultaneously cut from $0.0015 / $0.002 per 1k to $0.001 / $0.002 per 1k. Announced at OpenAI DevDay November 6, 2023.

events.title: GPT-4o launch — $5 / $15 per 1M tokens; 2x cheaper than GPT-4 Turbo input
events.detail: GPT-4o (gpt-4o) launched at $5 per 1M input tokens and $15 per 1M output tokens — half the input price of GPT-4 Turbo at the same quality tier. Announced at OpenAI Spring Update on May 13, 2024.

events.title: GPT-4o mini launch — $0.15 / $0.60 per 1M tokens (replaces GPT-3.5-Turbo)
events.detail: GPT-4o mini launched as the new low-cost frontier model at $0.15 per 1M input and $0.60 per 1M output — roughly 30× cheaper than GPT-4o on input. OpenAI simultaneously deprecated GPT-3.5-Turbo for new users. GPT-4o mini became the go-to cheapest OpenAI model.

events.title: o3-mini and o1 family updates — reasoning model pricing established
events.detail: OpenAI released o3-mini as an affordable reasoning model. The o1 series pricing was also adjusted. Reasoning models introduced a new pricing tier above frontier chat models. NOTE: verify exact prices against Wayback captures.

gaps.reason: GPT-5 family model naming and pricing during 2025 H2 is beyond reliable training data for this window; current prices from models.json (verified 2026-06-20) reflect the current lineup.

tools.open_question: GPT-4o batch pricing (gpt-4o-2024-08-06 at 50% off announced 2024-10): when did the standard gpt-4o also get the cached input discount at $1.25/1M? Archive verification needed.

tools.name: Anthropic
tools.headline: Three Claude generations; Haiku anchors the cheap tier throughout

events.title: Claude 3 family launch — Haiku $0.25/$1.25, Sonnet $3/$15, Opus $15/$75 per 1M
events.detail: Claude 3 introduced three tiers: Haiku (fastest, cheapest) at $0.25 input / $1.25 output per 1M tokens; Sonnet (balanced) at $3 / $15; Opus (most capable) at $15 / $75. Haiku became one of the cheapest quality models in the market at launch.

events.title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet launch — same price ($3/$15) but significantly stronger model
events.detail: Claude 3.5 Sonnet launched at the same price point as Claude 3 Sonnet ($3 / $15 per 1M tokens) but with substantially better benchmarks — outperforming Claude 3 Opus on most tasks while costing 5x less. The price didn’t change; the value per dollar did.

events.title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet updated (Oct 2024 version) + Haiku 3.5 at $0.80/$4 per 1M
events.detail: An updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet (claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022) was released alongside Claude 3.5 Haiku at $0.80 per 1M input / $4 per 1M output — a ~3x increase over Claude 3 Haiku's $0.25/$1.25 but with substantially higher capability. Claude 3 Haiku remained available at original price.

events.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet launch — hybrid reasoning model, $3/$15 per 1M
events.detail: Claude 3.7 Sonnet introduced a hybrid reasoning mode (extended thinking) at the same $3 / $15 per 1M price point as previous Sonnet models. Extended thinking tokens billed at output token rate.

events.title: Claude 4 family announced — new Opus/Sonnet generation
events.detail: Anthropic announced the Claude 4 family. NOTE: exact pricing and model lineup at announcement need verification against official Anthropic pricing page and Wayback captures from May 2025.

gaps.reason: Claude 4 and 4.x family launch pricing between May 2025 and June 2026 is beyond reliable training data; current prices from models.json (verified 2026-06-20).

tools.name: Google (Gemini)
tools.headline: Flash tier anchors lowest frontier API price; 2.0 and 2.5 generation shipped free-then-paid

stable.detail: frontier tier, 1M token context, long-context surcharge >200k tokens

events.title: Gemini 1.0 Pro API general availability — pricing announced
events.detail: Google announced Gemini 1.0 Pro for general availability via the Gemini API (formerly PaLM API). Pay-as-you-go pricing introduced. Gemini 1.0 Pro was priced below GPT-4 at launch. NOTE: verify exact prices against Wayback captures.

events.title: Gemini 1.5 Pro and Flash launch — 1M token context; Flash as cheap tier
events.detail: Gemini 1.5 Pro launched with 1M token context window. Gemini 1.5 Flash was introduced as a lightweight, fast, cheaper model at $0.35 per 1M input / $1.05 per 1M output (prompts up to 128k tokens) — establishing the Flash sub-brand as Google’s cheap-tier offering. 1.5 Pro was $3.50 / $10.50 (up to 128k). Long-context surcharges applied above thresholds.

events.title: Gemini 2.0 Flash Experimental — free preview period
events.detail: Gemini 2.0 Flash Experimental was released for free during the experimental/preview period. Paid pricing was not yet published; developers could use it at no cost through the Gemini API free tier.

events.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash launch — new generation pricing
events.detail: Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Flash launched. Flash continued as the low-cost option in the 2.5 lineup. NOTE: exact prices at launch need verification against official Google pricing page and Wayback captures from March 2025.

gaps.reason: Gemini 3.x family pricing is beyond reliable training data; current prices from models.json (verified 2026-06-20).

tools.open_question: When did Gemini Flash transition from free experimental to paid? Exact date and price announcement need Wayback verification.

events.title: DeepSeek-R1 and V3 API launch — ~30x cheaper than GPT-4o on input
events.detail: DeepSeek-R1 (reasoning model) and DeepSeek-V3 launched as API products. Prices were dramatically lower than Western competitors: DeepSeek-V3 at approximately $0.27 per 1M input / $1.10 per 1M output; DeepSeek-R1 at approximately $0.55 per 1M input / $2.19 per 1M output. Compared to GPT-4o at $5/$15, this represented roughly 10–18x cheaper input pricing. The launch caused significant industry discussion and competitor pricing pressure.

gaps.reason: DeepSeek did not have a widely-available Western API before January 2025; no pricing history to track for this window.
DeepSeek V4 family pricing is beyond reliable training data; current prices from models.json (verified 2026-06-20).

tools.name: Mistral
tools.headline: Mistral Large dropped dramatically from 2024 to 2025; full lineup expanded to 11 models

events.title: Mistral API initial pricing — Mistral Large at ~$8/$24 per 1M
events.detail: Mistral launched its commercial API with Mistral Large (then called Mistral Large 2) at approximately $8 per 1M input / $24 per 1M output. Mistral Medium and Small were also available at lower prices. Exact prices at launch need Wayback verification.

events.title: Mixtral 8x7B and 8x22B mixture-of-experts models — different pricing tier
events.detail: Mistral released the Mixtral series (mixture-of-experts architecture) which had different pricing from the dense Mistral Large models. Mixtral was positioned as a high-performance, more affordable alternative. NOTE: exact prices need Wayback verification.

events.title: Mistral Large price cut — from ~$2/$6 to $2/$6 per 1M (Mistral Large 2)
events.detail: By late 2024, Mistral had reduced Mistral Large pricing significantly from the initial launch prices. The model available as 'Mistral Large' by this period was Mistral Large 2 at approximately $2 / $6 per 1M tokens. NOTE: verify exact prices and dates against Wayback captures.

events.title: Mistral Large 3 replaces Large 2 — price drop to $0.50/$1.50 per 1M
events.detail: WizardCost verification (2026-06-20) found the current 'Mistral Large' model is Mistral Large 3 at $0.50 per 1M input / $1.50 per 1M output — a dramatic reduction from Mistral Large 2's $2/$6. Our data was one generation behind; updated in models.json on 2026-06-20.

gaps.reason: Mistral pricing evolution between Mixtral launch and Mistral Large 3 availability is not fully traceable from available training data; key price cuts in this window need Wayback verification.

tools.open_question: Mistral Large 3 exact launch date and pricing at launch vs Mistral Large 2 retirement: when did the $2/$6 → $0.50/$1.50 transition happen? Wayback verification of mistral.ai/pricing needed.
